title: Demands and the cache mode
summary: A Demand has id, priority, ramMiB, pageableMiB (the part that may page; 0 means must not page), storageMiB, storageWhere (NONE LOCAL FABRIC), wantsRamSpeed, durability (READONLY TEMPORARY DURABLE) and cacheMode. The cache mode is decided case by case, per request (Tom Dyer, 2026-11-25): a request may name it; otherwise READONLY data gets a READONLY store, TEMPORARY a WRITEBACK cache, DURABLE a WRITETHROUGH cache. DURABLE data may not use WRITEBACK; a READONLY store needs READONLY data.
authority: built and tested offline (architecture Tom Dyer; coding and writing Claude (Opus 5.5), 2026-11-25)
invariants: The request decides its cache mode (Tom Dyer, 2026-11-25)
DURABLE data never uses a write-back cache
An unpageable demand never counts swap as RAM
procedure: Give every demand its real pageable part; it decides whether swap can help
